hero.title: Nature-Climate Policy Coherence Analyzer
hero.subtitle: Where national climate, biodiversity, and land-use policies align, and where they may pull in different directions.

inside.title: Every policy target, mapped against every other
inside.body: Each ribbon links two national policy documents. Green shows where their targets are in strong alignment; red threads mark a potential misalignment worth a closer look.
inside.disclaimer: AI-generated analysis. Treat as a prompt to review, not a settled finding.

step2.title: Automated analysis

step3.title: Explore results

legend.warmerArcHint: Warmer arcs mark documents with more potential misalignment.
legend.ribbonWidth: Ribbon width shows the number of scored pairs the two documents share.

arcs.title: The coloured arcs are policy documents
arcs.body: Each arc on the outer rim is one policy document (or one sector, depending on the view). Longer arcs contain more targets.

ribbons.title: Ribbons connect documents
ribbons.body: Each ribbon links two documents whose targets were compared. Green shows pairs that support each other; the dashed red share shows pairs flagged as potential misalignments. Wider ribbons mean more compared pairs. These links are AI-estimated prompts for review, not verdicts.

labels.title: Labels name each document
labels.body: A thin guide line points from each arc to its name. Clicking a label or its arc focuses the wheel on that document.

docToggle.title: Choose which documents you see
docToggle.body: This colour key is also a filter: click a document to add it to or remove it from the picture. The colours match the arcs on the wheel.

grid.title: One cell per document pair
grid.body: Each cell compares the targets of its row document with its column document. Click a cell to open the details for that pair.

diagonal.title: The diagonal stays blank
diagonal.body: Cells on the diagonal would compare a document with itself, so they are left empty.

colours.title: Green and red show the balance
colours.body: Greener cells have a larger share of mutually supportive target pairs; redder cells have a larger share flagged as potential misalignments. These comparisons are AI-estimated starting points for review.

intensity.title: Stronger colour, further from typical
intensity.body: Colour strength shows how far a pair sits from the typical level across all the documents shown here. Pale cells are close to typical; deep colours are the outliers worth a closer look.

source.title: What this budget data is
source.body: This names the spending review the figures come from — the country, the period, and the budget lines it covers. Open the list to inspect every budget line.

concentration.title: Where the money concentrates
concentration.body: This breakdown shows how the reviewed spending is distributed across areas, next to how many policy targets sit in each. Areas that carry targets but no recorded budget are listed as well.

execution.title: Planned versus actually spent
execution.body: This bar compares planned spending with what was actually spent, over the programme's own period — which can be wider than the review period above.

statusKey.title: The dots are reported actions
statusKey.body: Each dot is one action from the country's own report, coloured by its reported status — from planned (hollow) through to implemented (green).

rows.title: One row per institution
rows.body: Each row lists an institution the report names, with its actions shown as dots. Click a row to read those actions one by one.

caveat.title: Read the counts with care
caveat.body: An action that names several institutions counts once for each of them, so the numbers show involvement — not shares of the work, and never a ranking.

institutions.title: Institutions on the left
institutions.body: Each bar on the left is an institution the country's report names on reported actions. Taller bars carry more actions.

ribbons.title: Ribbons show where effort lands
ribbons.body: Each ribbon connects an institution to a policy document its reported actions relate to. Wider ribbons mean more matched targets. These matches are AI-estimated and meant for review.

documents.title: Documents on the right
documents.body: Each bar on the right is a policy document, in the same colour it has across the rest of the briefing.

drilldown.title: Click a ribbon for the detail
drilldown.body: Selecting a ribbon lists the specific targets behind it, and each target opens the full explanation of the match.

bar.title: One bar, split by kind of friction
bar.body: The bar splits all flagged target pairs by the kind of friction involved. Each segment's width is that kind's share; click a segment to see where it plays out.

mechanisms.title: The three kinds, explained
mechanisms.body: Each column names one kind of friction, with its share, its count, and a short description of what it means.

total.title: The number behind the bar
total.body: This is the total number of target pairs flagged for review as potential misalignments — the pairs the bar splits by kind.

columns.title: Two columns of recurring themes
columns.body: The left column groups themes where documents mostly support one another; the right column groups themes flagged as potential misalignments. The themes are AI-derived groupings of related target pairs.

card.title: Each card is one theme
card.body: A card shows the theme's name, a short description, and how many target pairs sit behind it under the current selection. The thin bar compares that count with the other themes in its column.

interact.title: Explore a theme
interact.body: Click a card to open the detail with the pairs behind the theme. On larger screens, resting your pointer on a card previews the theme's documents on the wheel to the right.

switcher.title: Pick a document to focus on
switcher.body: These buttons switch the whole slide to one policy document. The headline and the list below update to that document's relationships.

pairs.title: The pairs worth reviewing
pairs.body: Each row is one target pair flagged as a potential misalignment between the focused document and a peer document. Click a row for the full explanation. These flags are AI-estimated prompts for review, not verdicts.

list.title: All document pairings, ranked
list.body: Each row is one pair of documents, ranked by how many target pairs were compared between them, with a short AI-written note on what the pattern is about.

balance.title: The green and red balance bar
balance.body: The bar's total length reflects how many target pairs were compared for the pairing; green is the share that support each other, red the share flagged as potential misalignments.

sync.title: The list and the matrix move together
sync.body: On larger screens, resting your pointer on a row lights up the matching cell in the coherence matrix to the right — and hovering a cell lights its row here. Click either to open the pair's detail.

lenses.title: Choose a grouping
lenses.body: These chips re-frame the table: group targets by a different sector classification, and choose whether to show supportive links, potential misalignments, or both.

columns.title: Two measures per sector
columns.body: "Targets" counts how many targets fall in the sector; "flagged share" is the portion of its reviewed pairs flagged for review. Click either heading to sort by it.

rows.title: One row per sector
rows.body: Each row is a sector with its two bars. Click a row to open the sector's detail; on larger screens, hovering highlights the sector on the wheel to the right.

flagShare.title: Reading the flagged-share bar
flagShare.body: The red bar shows the share of reviewed target pairs flagged as potential misalignments. The small dark tick marks the average across all sectors shown, so you can see which sectors sit above or below it.

bar.title: Most friction traces to a few targets
bar.body: Each coloured chunk is one target, sized by the flagged pairs it accounts for and coloured by its source document. The grey tail is every other target. Click a chunk to open that target's profile.

legend.title: What the numbers mean
legend.body: This line states how many targets carry what share of all flagged pairs, and what the grey area stands for.

list.title: The most contested targets
list.body: Each row is one target with the number of flagged pairs it appears in, shown as a bar scaled to the top target. Click a row for the full profile. These counts come from AI-flagged pairs and are review prompts, not findings.

legend.title: Reading the dots
legend.body: Each dot is one target in a document: filled means at least one reported action was matched to it; hollow means none was. These matches are AI-estimated.

dots.title: One map per document
dots.body: Every document lists its targets as dots in its own colour. Click a document to expand it and read the matched actions, the gaps, and the pairs to review.

review.title: The red review lane
review.body: A red bar and count appear when reported actions may pull against some of this document's targets. These are AI-estimated prompts for review, not findings.

provenance.method: The Biodiversity Expenditure Review (BER) identifies and quantifies biodiversity expenditure; it does not connect expenditure to policy targets. Every link shown here was made by the Tracker's AI, which compares each funding line's description with each target's text and judges how well they align.
provenance.caveat: AI-estimated alignment between descriptions — an indication of thematic association, not a record of money spent on a target.

methodNote.title: How these figures are produced
methodNote.intro: Biodiversity expenditure originates in public budget allocations implemented through institutions and programmes. The Biodiversity Expenditure Review (BER) identifies and quantifies that expenditure; it does not assign it to policy targets. The Tracker adds an analytical layer: its AI compares each programme's description with each policy target's text and records where the descriptions align. Each policy document above is therefore one analytical lens over the same reviewed expenditure — not an owner of it.
methodNote.q1Title: What counts as an aligned programme?
methodNote.q1Body: A budget programme whose description the Tracker's AI judged closely or moderately aligned with this target's text, and which recorded executed spend over the review period.
methodNote.q2Title: What if one programme aligns with several targets?
methodNote.q2Body: When a programme's description aligns with several targets, its full spend appears under each of them. A target's figure measures how much reviewed spending has descriptions aligned with that target — not money allocated to it.
methodNote.q3Title: How should per-target figures be read?
methodNote.q3Body: As a relative signal for comparing targets. They say nothing about whether financing is sufficient to achieve a target — that would require financing-needs and gap data this module does not include.
methodNote.q4Body: Per-target figures intentionally overlap. Wherever a total is shown for a document or for the review as a whole, each programme is counted once, so totals are not the sum of the per-target figures.
methodNote.coverageNote: The headline match count uses only closely aligned links; the dot grid and per-target figures also include moderately aligned links.

globeBreakdown.aiCaption: Categories are assigned by the Tracker's AI from each programme's description — they are not the national BIOFIN team's classification. Each programme counts once, under its main category. AI-estimated and indicative.

classification.heading: Thematic classification
classification.infoBox: Each policy target is classified against established taxonomies using AI. The climate mitigation taxonomy maps targets to standard IPCC emissions categories. The biodiversity taxonomy uses BIOFIN's GLOBE expenditure taxonomy to enable cross-level analysis. Targets may appear in multiple categories if they span several domains.
classification.provenanceMethod: Each target is scored by a large language model against every category in the active taxonomy ({taxonomy}). The chart shows primary-category counts; targets above the relevance threshold in additional categories are surfaced in click-through views.
classification.provenanceCaveat: Counts depend on which categories the model judged primary. Click a segment and inspect a few targets before treating shares as exhaustive; the model may split similar targets across adjacent categories.

contradictionDescription.goal_conflict: The objectives themselves pull against each other: achieving one substantively means not achieving the other.
contradictionDescription.resource_competition: The goals are compatible but compete for the same limited resource: land, water, budget, or capacity.

heading.title: Policy coherence explorer
heading.info: This visualization maps alignment relationships between policy targets across the documents. Lines between targets represent assessed relationships. Thicker, darker lines show stronger alignment. Dashed red lines indicate pairs the AI has identified as potential misalignment.
heading.infoScore: The coherency score is a quality-weighted percentage: each aligned pair scores 1 to 3 points (low/medium/high), divided by the maximum possible score.
heading.infoBtr: BTR node colors: reported mitigation measures are shown in violet and reported adaptation actions in fuchsia, so the two BTR subsets read apart at a glance.
heading.hoverHint: Hover or click a target to explore connections.

paradox.callout: {label} sits among both the most potentially misaligned and the most strongly aligned targets. Two sides of the same coin, worth a closer look.

zero_conflict_topic.callout: {category} carries zero potential misalignments across {size} targets, unusual when other topics carry {peak}+.

hub.callout: {label} aligns strongly with {docs} different documents, quietly bridging plans others touch separately.

orphan.callout: {label} has {connections, plural, =0 {no alignments or potential misalignments with any other target} other {only one connection across the whole dataset}}, isolated from the rest of the network.

imbalance.callout: {labelA} and {labelB} carry {contras} potential misalignments versus {aligns} strong alignments, the most lopsided pair in the dataset.
imbalance.pathway: A joint review across these two may help surface where their mandates diverge.

implementation_contradiction.callout: Reported action {btrLabel} ({status}) {severity, select, likely_conflict {is likely to conflict with} possible_conflict {may conflict with} other {may be misaligned with}} planned target {policyLabel}. What is being done versus what was planned.
implementation_contradiction.pathway: Reconciling the two, or flagging the pair for human review, could potentially close the gap between plan and practice.

most_contested_topic.callout: {category} carries {count} potential misalignments across {size} targets, the heaviest concentration in the dataset.

quantitative_gap.callout: {label} sits in {count} potential misalignments but carries no measurable indicator.
quantitative_gap.pathway: Without a number to anchor the target, several of these may rest on interpretation rather than policy conflict, worth a closer look before treating them as decision-grade signals.

agreement_pair.callout: {labelA} and {labelB} share {aligns} strong alignments and {contras, plural, =0 {zero potential misalignments} other {only # potential misalignments}}, the most cohesive pair in the dataset.

most_aligned_target.callout: {label} anchors {count} strong alignments, the single biggest connector in the dataset.

doc_most_tensions.callout: {docLabel} carries {count} potential misalignments, the heaviest concentration in any single document.

btr_status_mix.callout: {happening} of {total} reported actions are already Implemented or Ongoing, {adopt} Adopted and {plan} Planned. The Implemented and Ongoing share is the strongest signal of what is already happening on the ground.

quantitative_coverage.callout: Only {quant} of {total} targets carry a measurable indicator. The rest read as direction-of-travel statements, hard to track without a number to anchor them.
quantitative_coverage.pathway: Many of the alignment and potential-misalignment counts here may carry more interpretive weight than substantive policy conflict, given how many targets are direction-of-travel statements.

anchor_support_gap.callout: {pillarLabel} has {count, plural, =0 {no strong supporting alignments from other plans} =1 {only one strong alignment from other plans} other {only # strong alignments from other plans}}, the least-supported pillar in this dataset.
anchor_support_gap.pathway: Reviewing whether existing targets in other plans could be mapped to this pillar may surface under-claimed alignment with the national plan.

sector_coverage_gap.callout: Sector "{sector}" carries {count} policy targets but no reported actions in BTR, the largest plan-vs-practice gap by sector in this dataset.
sector_coverage_gap.pathway: Cross-checking whether the gap reflects missing implementation or missing transparency reporting may help close the loop.

lulucfExplainer.heading: About negative LULUCF values:
lulucfExplainer.body: The Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry sector shows negative numbers because Mongolia's forests and grasslands currently absorb more CO₂ than they emit, making this sector a net carbon sink. In international GHG accounting, removals from the atmosphere are reported as negative values. A value becoming less negative (moving toward zero) means the sink is weakening and absorbing less carbon over time, which is a warning sign for climate goals.

financingCoherence.heading: Budget & Financing Coherence
financingCoherence.barChartNote: A bar-chart view disaggregated by ministry will follow once the BER program-to-ministry mapping is wired (separate workstream).

infoBox.intro: How government biodiversity expenditure aligns with policy commitments and reported actions, grouped by a shared taxonomy. Each row shows how much budget is allocated, how many policy targets address the category, and how many BTR-reported actions fall under it.
infoBox.detail: The BIOFIN GLOBE view uses BIOFIN's official framework for Biodiversity Expenditure Reviews (48 subcategories grouped into 9 primary categories). The Climate Mitigation view uses the IPCC sector taxonomy. Subcategory assignments are generated by an LLM classifier calibrated on expert examples. All monetary values in {currency} ({period}).

provenance.method: Expenditure values come directly from the uploaded BER. Each program is then assigned to one BIOFIN GLOBE category (or IPCC mitigation sector) by an LLM classifier from the program's description.
provenance.caveat: The BER is a subset of national expenditure; only programs flagged in the uploaded review are shown. Totals here do not represent the country's full budget. Coverage depends entirely on what was uploaded; programs not in the BER are invisible to this section.

Actions that don't map to any biodiversity category appear under "Not classified".

targetAtlas.title: Target atlas
targetAtlas.infoBox: Items are connected when they share a relevant category in the selected lens. Horizontal = # cross-doc policy targets sharing a category. Vertical = # BTR actions + # BER programmes sharing a category. Red ring = LLM-flagged possible misalignments with other targets. See “How to read this” below the header for the full story.
targetAtlas.provenanceMethod: Each dot is a policy target. Connections are inferred from LLM taxonomy classifications under the selected lens; the red ring comes from the same LLM pairwise alignment pass used by the coherency views. BTR actions and BER programmes contribute to the vertical <quoted>backing</quoted> axis only when they share a lens category with a target.
targetAtlas.provenanceCaveat: Both axes depend on the chosen lens; switching lenses recomputes positions. The Atlas shows semantic coherence (shared categories), not material flows of money or implementation effort.
targetAtlas.lensSelectTitle: The connecting taxonomy. Two items are linked (on both axes) if they share a relevant category.
targetAtlas.intro: Every dot is a policy target from the national documents (NDC, NBSAP, NAP, …). Its position reflects two relationships, both seen through the Lens chosen above: how the target relates to other policies, and how it relates to reported government action and the national budget. Click any dot for details.
targetAtlas.introNoBer: No BER (budget) data for this country, so the vertical axis reflects reported action only.
targetAtlas.introNoBtr: No BTR (reported action) data, so the vertical axis reflects budget only.
targetAtlas.howToReadSummary: How to read this – and what it answers
targetAtlas.htrPositionTitle: How a target gets its position
targetAtlas.htrPositionBody: Every target, every reported action (BTR), and every budget programme (BER) is tagged with categories from a shared taxonomy: the Lens. Two items are linked when they share at least one tag. No human hand-picks these links, and no single opaque score drives position.
targetAtlas.htrHorizontal: Horizontal (coherence) counts linked policy targets in other documents. Further right = the same idea comes up again and again across the policy stack.
targetAtlas.htrVertical: Vertical (backing) combines linked BTR actions and BER programmes, weighted: BTR by reported execution stage, BER by spend relative to the country average. Further up = stronger evidence of action and budget in the same area.
targetAtlas.htrRedRing: Red ring marks targets with many potential misalignments only: those the AI has identified as potentially misaligned with 5 or more other policy targets. Targets with fewer aren't ringed, to keep the chart readable; every potentially misaligned pair is still listed in the side panel when a dot is clicked. Potential misalignments sit alongside the axes, not subtracted from them. A target can be strongly aligned and potentially misaligned.
targetAtlas.htrOrphansNote: Only targets that carry at least one tag in the current lens are shown. Turn on <quoted>Hide lens-orphans</quoted> to remove targets pinned to the origin because this lens doesn't apply to them (e.g. public-health targets under a biodiversity lens).
targetAtlas.htrQuadWellSupported: Well-supported (top right): linked to many other policy targets and to reported action or budget. The country's policy stack and its implementation/financing machinery both back this target. e.g. a renewable-energy target that recurs across NDC, NBSAP and NAP and is covered by BTR mitigation measures and a BER programme.
targetAtlas.htrQuadAmbitionGap: Ambition gap (bottom right): echoed across many policies, but no reported action and no budget programme touches the same area. The classic say-do gap. e.g. a pollinator-habitat restoration target that several documents mention but no BTR action or BER programme covers.
targetAtlas.htrQuadBackedIsolated: Backed but isolated (top left): reported action or budget is there, but few other policy targets reinforce it. The country is doing or paying for something that stands on its own. e.g. an anti-desertification budget line that isn't strongly echoed in NBSAP, NDC or NAP.
targetAtlas.htrQuadLimitedUptake: Limited uptake (bottom left): few cross-policy links, few reported actions, few budget programmes in this area. Could be a strategic orphan, a very narrow target, or a poor fit for this lens. Worth a direct read before judging.
targetAtlas.htrLinksTitle: What each kind of link shows
targetAtlas.htrLinkPolicy: Link to another policy target → two documents contain objectives that fall in the same thematic area. They reinforce each other.
targetAtlas.htrLinkBtr: Link to a BTR action → the country's Biennial Transparency Report lists a mitigation measure or adaptation action in the same thematic area. It means the country is already doing something related to this target.
targetAtlas.htrLinkBer: Link to a BER programme → a named budget line in the Biodiversity Expenditure Review funds activity in the same thematic area. The country is already paying for something related. It's a count of programmes, not a currency amount; dollar totals per category live in the Financing Coherence section below.
targetAtlas.htrLensBody: A target classified as <quoted>Restoration</quoted> in GLOBE may be classified as <quoted>LULUCF</quoted> under IPCC sector and <quoted>Forest management</quoted> under NBS. Each lens re-wires the network of shared tags, so the same target can move from edge to centre under a different lens. This supports cross-checking: a target that looks isolated under one lens but load-bearing under another points to a framing difference rather than a gap.
targetAtlas.htrAuditBody: Click any dot. The side panel lists the shared tags connecting it to every linked programme and action, alongside a second, independent LLM-generated alignment score. Where the two agree, confidence is high. Where they disagree, surface for discussion. The tags are the authoritative link; the LLM read is a cross-check.

visionAnchorCoverage.heading: Operationalising {anchor}
visionAnchorCoverage.infoBoxIntro: How does the rest of the country's policy stack relate to {anchorFull}? Each row is one {anchor} ambition; each column is a peripheral document. Bar segments show the strength of the AI-assessed relationships between each ambition and the targets in that document, colored by the seven-level alignment scale (only the levels present in the data are shown).
visionAnchorCoverage.infoBoxNote: These policy documents contain no outright conflicts flagged with {anchor}; the only friction signal the model emits here is possible misalignment. The default sort surfaces ambitions with the weakest operational backing first, since that is the actionable gap.
visionAnchorCoverage.provenanceMethod: Each pair of (Vision target, peripheral target) is scored by an LLM on a seven-level alignment scale. Counts shown in each cell are aggregations of those per-pair judgements.
visionAnchorCoverage.provenanceCaveat: Single-model judgements skew toward 'medium' alignment. Read the per-pair rationale in the click-through modals before treating any cell as a settled finding.
visionAnchorCoverage.subtitleMatrix: {rows} {anchor} ambitions compared against {peripheral} peripheral targets across {docs} documents. Click a cell to read the underlying targets and AI rationale.
visionAnchorCoverage.subtitleSunburst: {anchor} sits at the center; the inner ring shows each ambition tinted by its status, the outer ring shows each ambition's alignment-level distribution. Hover any wedge to focus, click to drill in, click an outer slice to read the underlying targets.
visionAnchorCoverage.subtitleLoose: Peripheral targets whose strongest link to any {anchor} ambition is "low" or "possible misalignment" only. They may operationalise priorities outside {anchor}'s long-term framing, or signal where {anchor} itself does not yet capture an emerging priority.
visionAnchorCoverage.noRecordsAtLevel: No peripheral records at this alignment level.
visionAnchorCoverage.looseEmpty: Every peripheral target reaches at least medium-or-better alignment with one {anchor} ambition. No loosely-connected targets surface in this dataset.
visionAnchorCoverage.orphanDescription: The model judged this target unrelated to every Vision 2050 ambition. May operationalise priorities outside Vision 2050's framing.
visionAnchorCoverage.possibleMisalignmentLinks: {count, plural, one {# possible-misalignment link} other {# possible-misalignment links}}
visionAnchorCoverage.lowAlignmentLinks: {count, plural, one {# low-alignment link} other {# low-alignment links}}
visionAnchorCoverage.rowModalTitle: {id} · {count, plural, one {# peripheral record} other {# peripheral records}}

tension_heavy.label: Misalignment-heavy
tension_heavy.description: Possible-misalignment links dominate the relationships with this ambition. Worth examining where the friction comes from.

sparse_strong_support.label: Sparse strong support
sparse_strong_support.description: Few peripheral targets reach medium-or-better alignment with this ambition. May indicate a coverage gap.

single_doc_dependency.label: Single-document dependency
single_doc_dependency.description: All medium-or-better operationalisation comes from a single peripheral document; concentration risk if that document's priorities shift.

diversified_backing.label: Diversified backing
diversified_backing.description: At least three peripheral documents contribute medium-or-better operationalisation of this ambition.
